exercises.title: Elicitation planning 1 — prepare, perform or follow up?
exercises.problemHtml:
Wiegers splits each elicitation activity into preparing (scope and agenda, resources, learn about the stakeholders, questions, straw-man models), performing (educate stakeholders about the approach, take good notes, use the physical space) and following up (organise and share the notes, document open issues).

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Chuẩn bị · thực hiện · theo dõi sau buổi khai thác.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Elicitation planning 3 — the elicitation plan
exercises.problemHtml:
A project-level elicitation plan covers: objectives (overall and per activity); strategy and techniques (which technique for which stakeholder group, depending on access); schedule and resource estimates (participants, BA preparation and follow-up time); documents and systems needed for independent elicitation; expected products; and elicitation risks.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Elicitation planning 4 — notes and open issues
exercises.problemHtml:
Organise and share the notes soon after the session: consolidate sources, update while fresh, keep the raw notes, and ask participants to review. Record each open issue in the issue tracker with notes, an owner and a due date.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.
